A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 31 readable pages, including appendices A–E, Tables 1–13, and Figures 1–18. Textual and visual inspection supports a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original completion experiments, baseline comparisons, architectural ablations, and mesh reconstruction evaluations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the original experimental results, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, per-class scores, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same encoder, object-center and seed-offset generator, scene-constraint attention, decoder, normal prediction, mesh reconstruction, and training loss.

E1.justification: Both retain ShapeNet pretraining and chair ablations, ScanWCF instance and scene completion, and real ScanNet generalization examples in Appendix E.6. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: RfD-Net and DIMR remain the scene-completion comparators. The modified SeedFormer baseline in Table 3 and PCA normal-estimation comparators with k=16, 32, and 48 in Table 13 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the reported 946/246-scene training/test split, two partial scans per scene, training budgets, model sizes, metrics and thresholds, and evaluations using predicted or ground truth instance masks.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 and Appendix E retain the same architectural, scene-constraint, and pretraining ablations, plus analyses of input incompleteness, segmentation errors, real-scan generalization, normal estimation, and failure cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Aggregate-score reporting and the averaging description for Figure 12 are unchanged.

E6.justification: All matched numerical and qualitative results are unchanged, including Tables 1–13, Figure 12 trends, and Appendix E.1 runtime. For example, Table 2 reports CD 20.74 and COL 2.67 for the pretrained proposed model in both versions.

T1.justification: The model and loss equations in Section 3 and metric definitions in Appendix D are mathematically unchanged, including the collision formula. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning completion under arbitrary pose and scale, sparse scene constraints, ScanWCF, and improved completion quality, partial-scan fidelity, and collision avoidance.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of architectural and pretraining benefits and the same limitations concerning deterministic output, extremely sparse inputs, segmentation errors, and collisions in unobserved regions.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices B–D retain the same hyperparameters, hardware, training times, architecture dimensions, Mask3D/NKSR setup, data construction, and preprocessing details. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The citations and reference list match. Section 2 retains the same positioning relative to object-level and scene-level completion, including SCARP, DDIT, and PaSCo.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 8 April 2025 to v2 dated 9 March 2026. The paper's prose, terminology, headings, and section and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–18 and Tables 1–13 retain the same displays, captions, labels, structure, and placement. The page layout is unchanged; the version-stamp text update is covered under P1.

improvement.justification: The full papers, including appendices, retain the same scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and visual presentation. The updated arXiv version/date labeling does not meaningfully improve or diminish clarity, evidential support, or reproducibility.
